title: OpenChainGraph v0.4 — artifact envelope + catalog node object
description: NORMATIVE machine schema for OpenChainGraph v0.4. Source of truth pairs with standard/SPEC.md. spec_version of record lives in chaingraph.json.spec_version. Strict (additionalProperties:false) on BOTH the artifact envelope and the catalog node object: chaingraph.json is a single-producer internal catalog in this repo, so the forward-compat case for permissive request bodies does not apply — strictness catches our own typo/drift fields. Adding a new node field = a one-line schema update in the same PR.

citationRef.description: A minimal pointer to another legal instrument — the shape used by superseded_by. scheme + id only; the full pinned object lives wherever that instrument is itself cited.

regulatoryCitation.description: CLAUSE BINDING §1.2 pinned citation object, profile ocg-clause-binding@1. The PINNED form of a regulatory citation, replacing the legacy bare string. The legacy ["string"] form stays VALID and conformant but is classified UNPINNED (§1.1) and is ineligible for any pinned-form guarantee. This object is only PINNED when it sits inside the JCS-canonical execution_hash preimage — a member of policy_parameters or output_payload (§1.4); a copy of it anywhere else is unpinned no matter how well-formed it is. scheme is an OPEN enum on purpose (§1.2): ELI does not cover US CFR, Basel paragraph ids, or Fed SR letters, so requiring an ELI/AKN URI would exclude most of this estate. Shape only is validated here; the pointer-is-inside-the-preimage rule and the interpretation_ref content-hash rule are enforced by clause-binding.test.mjs.

scheme.description: Identifier scheme. Suggested values: cfr, eli, akn, bcbs-para, sr-letter, esma-vr, uscode, other. Deliberately NOT a closed enum.

path.description: Paragraph/subsection within the instrument, e.g. "(e)(3)". Presence of a real path is what makes a citation L2 rather than L1 (§1.3).

uri.description: Resolvable publisher URI, when one exists.

in_force_from.description: ISO date the cited text took legal force. A bare 4-digit schedule/version year is NOT this (§1.3).

in_force_to.description: ISO date the cited text ceased to be in force, or null while it remains in force.

governing_law.description: Governing law of the agreement the mapping serves, e.g. "US-NY". Distinct from jurisdiction on purpose.

superseded_by.description: The instrument that replaced this one. Recording supersession is ADDITIVE; a superseded citation is never silently stripped (§12).

mapped_by.description: Attributed identity of whoever made the clause-to-computation mapping. Required: an unattributed mapping is not a pinned mapping.

mapped_at.description: ISO date the mapping was made. A dated observation expires honestly; it promises nothing about the future.

interpretation_ref.description: Content hash of the interpretation document behind the mapping. MUST be a content hash, never a URL or a registry key (§0.10).

clauseBinding.description: CLAUSE BINDING §1.4 declaration, profile ocg-clause-binding@1. Lives at the top-level clause_bindings array. Attached AFTER hashing and EXCLUDED from execution_hash scope (like §20 anchor_bindings, §23 input_attestations, §25 private_inputs) — the array is a machine-readable index, NOT the binding. The binding itself is the §1.2 citation object sitting inside the preimage that execution_hash already covers. pointer is an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer that MUST start at /policy_parameters or /output_payload; that restriction is §1.4 made mechanical, so a citation outside the signed preimage cannot claim pinned status through this array. Zero entries is byte-identical to a plain artifact and fully conformant: this profile applies to newly-minted artifacts only and migrates nothing.

pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer, rooted at the artifact, naming where the §1.2 citation object lives INSIDE the execution_hash preimage. Any other root is a §1.4 violation and fails this pattern.

profile.description: Optional explicit profile tag. Omitted means the same thing: entries in this array are ocg-clause-binding@1 by definition.

privateInputDeclaration.description: OCG Standard §25 Private-Input declaration — names a policy_parameters location that holds a HIDING COMMITMENT instead of cleartext, under a named commitment scheme. Optional; lives at the top-level private_inputs array. Attached AFTER hashing, EXCLUDED from execution_hash scope (like §20 anchor_bindings and §23 input_attestations) — the array is a machine-readable index, not the binding: the binding is the commitment sitting inside policy_parameters (in the §4 preimage) plus the §18 journal. pointer is an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into policy_parameters; the value it resolves to MUST BE the commitment string (never plaintext) — §25.2 plaintext-exclusion. commitment is a sha256:-prefixed hiding commitment = SHA-256(salt ‖ cgCanon(input)); the ≥256-bit salt is prover-held disclosure material and NEVER appears in the artifact. This schema validates shape only; plaintext-exclusion + scheme validity + the journal-commits-the-commitment binding are enforced by validate-private-inputs.test.mjs (with the §18 pairing check in compute-proof.test.mjs).

pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into policy_parameters naming the private input. The value it resolves to MUST be the commitment (§25.2).

commitment.description: The hiding commitment SHA-256(salt ‖ cgCanon(input)); sha256:-prefixed. This same string is what sits at pointer inside policy_parameters.

commitment_scheme.description: The commitment construction. sha256-salted@1 is the sole scheme in this profile version; a new construction ships as ocg-private-input@<n>, never an in-place edit (§25.7).

inputAttestation.description: OCG Standard §23 Input Attestation — portable per-input evidence that a named input value was vouched for by an external source. Optional; lives at the top-level input_attestations array. Attached AFTER hashing, EXCLUDED from execution_hash scope (like §16 audit_signature and §20 anchor_bindings). pointer is an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer evaluated against policy_parameters (naming WHICH input). Types vc-2.0 / c2pa-manifest / rfc3161-snapshot verify with shipped §16/§13.11/§20 machinery; zktls is defined with EXTERNAL verification (no vendored verifier). This schema validates shape only; digest binding + cryptographic verification are enforced by validate-input-attestations.test.mjs.

pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into policy_parameters naming the attested input.

proof.description: The attestation payload. vc-2.0 = a W3C VC 2.0 credential object; rfc3161-snapshot = base64 verbatim RFC 3161 TST DER; c2pa-manifest = the C2PA manifest (object or base64); zktls = an opaque zkTLS proof string.

source_ref.description: Issuer DID / URL / TLS origin string naming who vouches. Informative to the trust decision, never a substitute for verifying proof.

anchorBinding.description: OCG Standard §20 Anchor Binding — portable, offline-verifiable evidence that execution_hash was included in a transparency log or timestamp service by a point in time. Optional; lives at the top-level anchor_bindings array. Attached AFTER hashing, EXCLUDED from execution_hash scope (like §16 audit_signature). anchored_hash MUST equal the artifact's execution_hash (enforced by anchor-binding.test.mjs; this schema validates shape). rfc3161-tst carries four additional REQUIRED members; the DER in proof is stored verbatim, never re-encoded.

proof.description: tlog-proof@v1 text | base64 COSE receipt (carries its own inclusion proof).

buildIdentity.description: OCG Standard §17 Kernel Identity Binding — content digest of the kernel that produced the artifact. Optional; lives at audit_signature.build_identity. Hash-excluded; does not alter execution_hash or chaingraph_version. An advisory published claim of which kernel SOURCE ran (not a proof of execution — that is §18).

buildType.description: Algorithm URI that produced the digest.

source_ref.description: Optional dereferenceable URL/commit pinning the source.

computeProof.description: OCG Standard §18 Compute-Integrity Proof — a zkVM receipt proving the named guest program produced output_payload. Optional; lives at audit_signature.compute_proof. Hash-excluded; does not alter execution_hash or chaingraph_version. System-agnostic; groth16-bn254 is the RECOMMENDED interop receipt form. Cryptographic seal-verification is DELEGATED to the named zkVM's vetted verifier (§18.1); this schema validates the binding shape only.

journal.description: Public outputs committed by the guest; MUST bind output_payload (§18.0).

dataIntegrityProof.description: OCG Standard §16 Proof Binding — a W3C Data Integrity proof (cryptosuite eddsa-jcs-2022) over the whole artifact (minus this proof). Optional; lives at audit_signature.proof. Hash-excluded; does not alter execution_hash or chaingraph_version. §16.5 (v0.7): optional id (referenceable by an endorsement) and previousProof (proof-chain endorsement — id(s) of the proof(s) this one countersigns).

proofSetOrChain.description: §16.5 (v0.7) — audit_signature.proof MAY be a single proof or an array (parallel proof set and/or previousProof endorsement chain).

sha256ref.description: Either a bare 64-char hex digest or a sha256:-prefixed digest.

merkleInclusion.description: OCG Standard §20 (v0.8) — OPTIONAL member on rfc3161-tst / opentimestamps anchor bindings. Batch anchoring: the artifact execution_hash is a LEAF of an RFC 6962 tree whose ROOT is the anchored value, so one timestamp covers many artifacts. When present a verifier MUST reconstruct the root from leaf+path and require root == anchored_hash AND leaf == artifact execution_hash (anchor-binding.test.mjs).

leaf.description: The artifact execution_hash (a tree leaf entry).

decisionGate.description: OCG Standard §21.4 (v0.8) — OPTIONAL decision gate on a chain step. Evaluated against THIS step's output_payload; routes control FORWARD (a later step id or "end"). First-match; default REQUIRED (total function). Closed op enum; strict typing, no coercion. Static-validated by validate-chains (forward-only, targets resolve, no unreachable step); evaluated by the shared kernels/_gateval.mjs on every surface. gate_policy/gate_threshold (v0.8.12, §27.4) are OPTIONAL additive fields carrying the §27 human-accountability precondition; a gate with neither evaluates byte-identically to a pre-§27 gate — the routing math in rules/default is untouched.

input.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into this step's output_payload.

value.description: Comparison operand (required for value ops; absent for present/absent). For gt/gte/lt/lte a finite number; for in a literal array.

next.description: Target step id or the literal "end". MUST be forward-only.

default.description: Target step id or "end" when no rule matches. REQUIRED and forward-only.

gate_policy.description: OPTIONAL §27.4 human-accountability precondition on this gate. Absent = pre-§27 gate, no precondition. When present and "dual_control", gate_threshold is REQUIRED (enforced by validate-ha-records.test.mjs, not by this shape schema).

gate_threshold.description: OPTIONAL §27.3 in-toto role+threshold pair this gate's dual_control(N) policy evaluates against. Only meaningful when gate_policy is "dual_control".

workMandateCondition.description: OCG Standard §22.1 (v0.8.1) — one threshold condition / escalation trigger inside a Work Mandate document. { pointer, op, value }: pointer is an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into a step's output_payload; op is the §21.4 closed gate-op enum; value is the operand (omitted for present/absent).

pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into a step's output_payload.

value.description: Comparison operand (required for value ops; absent for present/absent). For gt/gte/lt/lte a finite number; for in a literal array.

workMandateDocument.description: OCG Standard §22 (v0.8.1) — the output_payload of a Work Mandate artifact (mandate_type:"work_mandate"). SEPARATE from the frozen v0.4 artifact envelope ($defs/artifact) and NOT referenced by the top-level oneOf — additive, so it never alters existing artifact/catalog validation. A conformant Work Mandate is an $defs/artifact whose mandate_type is "work_mandate", whose output_payload matches this shape, and which carries a §16 eddsa-jcs-2022 proof (§22.2 — an unsigned mandate is a non-enforceable draft). scope authorizes nodes/chains; conditions name the auto-approval envelope; escalation_triggers route to the reserved "escalate" target (§22.3); validity bounds the window; principal is the signing authority.

scope.description: Authorized nodes and chains. At least one array MUST be non-empty (§22.1).

escalation_triggers.description: Conditions that route the run to the reserved "escalate" target (MAY be empty).

principal.description: The authorizing party. id is a did:key or LEI (§9); the §16 signature MUST verify against it.

anchor.description: OPTIONAL §20 anchor over the mandate hash (§22.2).

haGatePolicy.description: OCG Standard §27.4 (v0.8.12) — the closed human-accountability gate-policy vocabulary applied to a §21.4 decision gate as an OPTIONAL precondition. auto_pass = no human act; review_required = ≥1 reviewer approval; dual_control = §27.3 N-distinct-identity threshold (see haApprovalThreshold.threshold); escalate = route to the §22.3 reserved target; hold = suspend pending a human act; reject = terminal human rejection; emergency_override = §27.5 time-boxed override. Additive: the enum is consumed by the accountability layer as a precondition ANNOTATION; the §21.4 _gateval.mjs routing math is UNCHANGED.

haApprovalThreshold.description: OCG Standard §27.3 (v0.8.12) — an in-toto-style integer dual-control threshold: a gate is satisfied when ≥ threshold DISTINCT role-bound identities (counted by identity.id, NEVER by key) have each signed an `approval` record naming `role` over the same subject_hash. dual_control(2) is the N=2 case.

threshold.description: Number of DISTINCT approver identities required. A repeated identity counts once.

haRole.description: OCG Standard §27.1 (v0.8.12) — the closed set of human-accountability roles. approver is the legally-effective sign-off (attestor is its alias); examiner is READ-ONLY (grants inspection, never approval authority); checker (§27.12, v0.8.20) attests independent cross-org verification of someone else's already-sealed artifact, never organizational sign-off — distinct from reviewer/approver for that reason. A role binding ties one §9 identity to one role for one subject and MUST carry a §16 proof verifiable against that identity.

haPartyRole.description: OCG Standard §27.13 (v0.8.22) — the closed vocabulary carried by the OPTIONAL humanAccountabilityRecord.party_role sibling. Records a FACT about a party's pre-existing standing under the agreement the subject artifact reports on — never an authorization this record confers. signatory = the identity is a signatory to that agreement; observer = visibility but no signing authority under it; controlling_party = controlling standing over the matter at hand under that agreement (NEVER "controller" — that word reads as authority this record grants, and it grants none). Independent of haRole: a checker MAY be a signatory, an observer, or hold no party role at all. Inert by construction — no gate reads it, no §27.4 policy or §27.3 threshold counts over it. Closed: adding a value IS a spec change.

haRunState.description: OCG Standard §27.10 (v0.8.15) — the closed run-state vocabulary carried by the OPTIONAL humanAccountabilityRecord.subject_run_state sibling. ran = the subject was produced by an execution that completed, on inputs the acting party accepted as current (a positive claim, never a default); did_not_run = the computation, check, or control the subject stands for did NOT execute (the record evidences the absence itself, since an absent artifact cannot carry a field); ran_stale = produced from inputs already past their freshness bound (the accountability-side mirror of §23 freshness_status "stale"). ABSENCE MEANS NO CLAIM and MUST NOT be read as "ran". Closed: adding a value IS a spec change, because a verifier must not silently accept an unknown run-state and thereby treat it as ran. Closure is enforced by this enum under schema-validate; validate-ha-records.test.mjs asserts closure of record_type/haRole/haGatePolicy.

haKernelPin.description: OCG Standard §27.12 (v0.8.20) — the OPTIONAL humanAccountabilityRecord.kernel_pin sibling. Pins the producer a checker verified subject_hash against: kernel_digest for a §12 node subject, or tool_ref (the identical {tool_id, tool_version, entry, manifest_digest} shape §27's non-node attested-artifact clause already defines) for a chainless subject. Exactly one applies, matching whichever preimage produced subject_hash. Enters no execution_hash preimage; a verifier holding both the receipt and the kernel/tool source MAY confirm kernel_pin names the SAME producer the subject was actually produced against — a check this field's shape makes possible without asserting it was performed.

kernel_digest.description: §17 kernel identity, for a §12 node subject.

tool_ref.description: The §27 non-node attested-artifact producer pin, for a chainless subject.

haDelta.description: OCG Standard §27.14 (v0.8.23) — the OPTIONAL humanAccountabilityRecord.delta sibling. An itemized list of the field-level changes a cure or override record claims, DIGESTS ONLY, never raw values, so this field never re-opens what belongs in a preimage. Each entry names one changed field by RFC 6901 JSON Pointer plus the sha256 digest of its old and new value. A delta claiming a new value is a bare assertion unless a NEW sealed artifact carrying that value exists and is the thing this record's subject_hash cites via chain.parent_hashes, reusing the §21.6 ancestry-commitment pattern (this recompute supersedes that one). Enters no execution_hash preimage of the SUBJECT artifact; it is part of the approval record's own preimage like every other populated field on this object.

field_pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer to the changed field within the subject artifact's output_payload.

old_value_digest.description: sha256 digest of the field's value before the change. A digest, never the raw value.

new_value_digest.description: sha256 digest of the field's value after the change. A digest, never the raw value.

haReceiptTransitionType.description: OCG Standard §27.15 (v0.8.24) — the closed vocabulary carried by the OPTIONAL humanAccountabilityRecord.receipt_transition.type field. Describes this record's relationship to a PRIOR counter_signed_receipt (§27.12), named via the record's own subject_hash. countersign = the acting identity independently reproduced the prior receipt's own recomputation and reached the same result; challenge = the acting identity disputes the prior receipt (descriptive only, never opens or decides any dispute-resolution process); supersede = the acting identity treats this record as the operative one for the subject going forward, from its own point of view (the prior receipt is never deleted or invalidated); attest = the acting identity attests the prior receipt still holds as of a given instant, without re-performing the recomputation; extend = the acting identity extends how long IT will treat the prior receipt as current. Closed: adding, renaming, or letting a caller define a transition type IS a spec change, the same discipline record_type / haRole / haGatePolicy already carry. A verifier MUST reject an unrecognized value rather than silently accept it.

haReceiptTransition.description: OCG Standard §27.15 (v0.8.24) — the OPTIONAL humanAccountabilityRecord.receipt_transition sibling. MAY be present only when record_type is counter_signed_receipt, with subject_hash naming the PRIOR receipt's own execution_hash (§27.12's own reference mechanism, reused unchanged — no second extension path). Exactly the typed payload sub-object matching `type` MAY be populated; the other four MUST be absent. `consuming` is a property of the RECORD, never a lock: the acting identity's own claim about whether it now treats the prior receipt as no longer operative, governed by the same omit-not-false discipline as replay_verified (§27.12) — MUST be omitted where no claim is made, never set false. Inert by construction: no gate reads consuming or type, nothing executes a transition, no ordering is enforced between transitions on a receipt chain, and no valid-next-transition machinery exists. Vocabulary ban (binding, NORMATIVE): no field, description, or product copy describing a receipt_transition may use "accept", "acceptance", "settled", "final", or "finality" (or a settlement-implying synonym) — the same ban §27.12 and §27.13 already state.

consuming.description: OMIT-NOT-FALSE: absence means NO CLAIM, never set false to mean 'not consuming'.

countersign.description: Payload for type=countersign. Empty by design — the fact of independent reproduction is the whole payload, no field to add.

reason_code.description: Machine-stable token naming why the prior receipt is disputed. Never opens or routes any resolution process.

replacement_subject_hash.description: execution_hash of the artifact this record newly recomputed, which the acting identity treats as operative going forward. Recording this never deletes or invalidates the prior receipt.

as_of.description: ISO 8601 instant as of which the acting identity attests the prior receipt still holds, without independently recomputing it.

new_valid_until.description: ISO 8601 instant to which the acting identity extends its own treatment of the prior receipt as current. States the acting party's own future conduct, not a claim binding any other party.

humanAccountabilityRecord.description: OCG Standard §27.2 (v0.8.12) — the output_payload of a Human Accountability record artifact (mandate_type:"human_accountability_record"). SEPARATE from the frozen v0.4 artifact envelope ($defs/artifact) and NOT referenced by the top-level oneOf — additive, so it never alters existing artifact/catalog validation. A conformant approval record is an $defs/artifact whose mandate_type is "human_accountability_record", whose output_payload matches this shape, and which carries a §16 eddsa-jcs-2022 whole-artifact proof bound to the named human (§27.2 — an unsigned approval record is NOT conformant §27 evidence). It is a SCITT-style STATEMENT ABOUT A STATEMENT: it only REFERENCES the subject via subject_hash and never contains the subject's preimage, so it has ZERO impact on the subject artifact's execution_hash or canonicalization (§27.0 additivity). Shape only is validated here; additivity, threshold distinctness (§27.3), override expiry (§27.5), and the signed-named-human requirement are enforced by validate-ha-records.test.mjs (with the §16 pairing check in proof-binding.test.mjs).

record_type.description: §27.2 — the kind of accountable act this record evidences. counter_signed_receipt (§27.12, v0.8.20) is a cross-org peer verification: the checker independently recomputed the subject and signed a receipt of that recomputation — never organizational approval. cure (§27.14, v0.8.23) is a DISTINCT member from override: it evidences a regulatory cure-of-error correcting a prior artifact's value(s), never a time-boxed policy attenuation — do not conflate the two.

subject_hash.description: The execution_hash of the artifact being acted upon — the SCITT reference (§27.2). The record never contains the subject's preimage.

identity.description: The acting party (§9). id is a did:key or LEI; the §16 signature MUST verify against it. Threshold distinctness (§27.3) counts this id, never the signing key.

decision.description: OPTIONAL decision label where applicable (e.g. approve/reject). The record_type is the authoritative act.

subject_run_state.description: OPTIONAL §27.10 — whether the SUBJECT actually ran, as observed by the acting party. A SIBLING of record_type, deliberately not a record_type member: record_type names the human act, this names the machine state of the subject at the moment of that act. Additive and reporting-only — it enters NO subject execution_hash preimage, appears in no required[], never invalidates a structural/verifiable/execution_hash verdict, and changes no §21.4 routing math (a gate MAY target a copied-forward value). Absence is fully conformant and means NO CLAIM.

kernel_pin.description: OPTIONAL §27.12 (v0.8.20) — which kernel/tool a checker verified subject_hash against, so a receipt signed against the WRONG kernel is structurally detectable. A SIBLING of record_type, mirroring how §27.10 added subject_run_state: not required[], enters no execution_hash preimage, absence is fully conformant and means NO CLAIM (not merely that no pin was checked).

replay_verified.description: OPTIONAL §27.12 (v0.8.21) — true iff the checker independently re-ran the subject's computation deterministically and got a matching subject_hash before signing this record, never a rubber-stamp approval. A SIBLING of record_type, mirroring kernel_pin and subject_run_state: not required[], enters no execution_hash preimage. Governed by §27.4's existing omit-not-false discipline: where no replay was attempted, the field MUST be omitted, never set false — false would read as an attempted replay that disagreed. Absence is fully conformant and means NO CLAIM.

party_role.description: OPTIONAL §27.13 (v0.8.22) — the acting identity's standing under the agreement the subject artifact reports on (signatory/observer/controlling_party), a FACT about the parties' own prior agreement, never an authorization this record grants. A THIRD sibling of record_type, mirroring kernel_pin and replay_verified: not required[], inert by construction — no gate reads it. Independent of role (§27.1): a checker MAY hold any party_role or none. Absence means NO CLAIM about standing.

delta.description: OPTIONAL §27.14 (v0.8.23) — an itemized array of field-level changes, digests only, that a cure or override record claims. A FOURTH sibling of record_type, mirroring kernel_pin, replay_verified, and party_role: not required[], enters no execution_hash preimage of the subject artifact. Available to both cure and override records. A delta claiming a new value is a bare assertion unless a new sealed artifact carrying it exists and is cited via subject_hash / chain.parent_hashes (§21.6 ancestry pattern). Absence means NO CLAIM about what changed.

receipt_transition.description: OPTIONAL §27.15 (v0.8.24) — a FIFTH sibling of record_type, mirroring kernel_pin/replay_verified/party_role/delta: not required[], enters no execution_hash preimage beyond the record's own. MAY be present only when record_type is counter_signed_receipt, with subject_hash naming the PRIOR receipt (§27.12's reference mechanism reused, no second extension path). Closed 5-value type vocabulary (countersign/challenge/supersede/attest/extend) with a typed payload per type; consuming is a property of the record's own claim, never an enforced lock. Absence means NO CLAIM.

gate_policy.description: OPTIONAL §27.4 gate policy this record satisfies or overrides.

reason_code.description: OPTIONAL machine-stable rationale token (REQUIRED by §27.5 for an override).

override.description: OCG Standard §27.5 — REQUIRED when record_type is "override": a time-boxed §22.10 attenuation. On expiry the override lapses and the underlying gate policy REVERTS (never a silent permanent auto-pass). scope narrows only, never widens (§22.10 / §SIDECAR.2).

scope.description: Which gate/subject the override covers (narrowing only).

expiry.description: ISO 8601 instant after which the override is treated as absent.

subject_hash.description: Immutable link to the overridden artifact's execution_hash.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 instant of the human act.

haEvidenceBundle.description: OCG Standard §27.6 (v0.8.12) — the accountability trail aggregated for one subject, exportable via §13 (and specifically §13.12 SD-JWT selective disclosure: approver identities + verdict always-disclosed, input values selectively disclosable, disclosure salts the sole permitted nondeterminism, never touching any execution_hash). A redacted bundle is NOT re-executable (§13.12 limitation) — it evidences the human trail, not a recomputation. submission_receipt is populated ONLY after a real transmission, never fabricated.

subject_hash.description: The §4 execution artifact this bundle documents.

kernel_version.description: §12/§17 build identity of the kernel that produced the subject.

reviewers.description: Reviewer identities paired with their signed approval-record hashes.

approvers.description: Approver identities paired with their signed approval-record hashes.

timestamps.description: Act timestamps, with OPTIONAL §20 anchor bindings.

submission_receipt.description: Populated only after a real transmission.

artifact.description: A v0.4 OpenChainGraph artifact. execution_hash = SHA-256(JCS({policy_parameters, output_payload})); the hash preimage is exactly those two members and nothing else.

@context.description: JSON-LD context. NOT version-locked to the spec number — v0.3 context is valid under v0.4 (export profiles are hash-excluded and add no PROV vocabulary).

chaingraph_version.description: MUST be 0.4.x for a v0.4 artifact.

compute_mode.description: New in v0.4 (§12). Excluded from the hash preimage.

mandate_type.description: §4 taxonomy (recommended) — prompt_template, payment_mandate, payment_policy, compliance_mandate, liquidity_mandate, capital_assessment, risk_control, settlement_mandate, infrastructure_mandate, credit_assessment, treasury_mandate, account_mandate, model_governance, attestation_mandate, cryptographic_mandate, aml_rule, risk_parameter, human_accountability_record (§27). NOT a hard enum: live nodes also use agent_guardrail_mandate / scheme_rule (the enum is not CI-enforced).

ancestry_digest.description: OCG Standard §21.6, new in v0.8.17 — OPTIONAL DAG-ancestry commitment, transitively covering order/membership/topology of the artifact's full ancestor sub-DAG. Hash-excluded (chain is outside the §4 preimage). Absence is fully conformant; no MUST-emit.

policy_parameters.description: Half of the hash preimage. Fold all decision inputs in here.

policy_parameters_hash.description: OCG Standard §PPH-1, new in v0.8.10 — OPTIONAL JCS-SHA-256 of policy_parameters alone, via the one canonical _hash.mjs path. EXCLUDED from the execution_hash preimage; purely additive, absence is conformant and carries no meaning.

supersedes.description: OCG Standard §1, new in v0.7 — OPTIONAL execution_hashes of artifacts this artifact corrects or replaces. Declared at creation; no reverse link, no status registry.

anchor_bindings.description: OCG Standard §20, new in v0.7 — OPTIONAL anchor-binding evidence entries. Attached after hashing; excluded from execution_hash scope.

retention_class.description: OCG Standard §20.3.0, new in v0.8.18 — OPTIONAL top-level artifact-level pruning-eligibility class, distinct from the per-attestation §23.4 input_attestations[].freshness.retention_class field of the same name (that field describes one attested input value's retention; this field describes the ARTIFACT'S OWN execution body). Governs §20.3.1 prune-behind-cosigned-checkpoint eligibility. Excluded from the execution_hash preimage; absence is fully conformant and is treated as case-file for §20.3 purposes.

input_attestations.description: OCG Standard §23, new in v0.8.3 — OPTIONAL per-input attestation entries. Attached after hashing; excluded from execution_hash scope. Zero attestations is fully conformant.

private_inputs.description: OCG Standard §25, new in v0.8.5 — OPTIONAL private-input declarations. Attached after hashing; excluded from execution_hash scope. Each entry names a policy_parameters pointer whose value is a hiding commitment (never plaintext). Zero entries is byte-identical to a plain v0.8.4 artifact and fully conformant.

clause_bindings.description: CLAUSE BINDING §1.4, profile ocg-clause-binding@1 — OPTIONAL declarations naming where §1.2 pinned citation objects sit INSIDE the execution_hash preimage. Attached after hashing; excluded from execution_hash scope. Zero entries is byte-identical to an artifact minted before this profile existed and is fully conformant — the profile applies to newly-minted artifacts only and migrates nothing.

node.description: A chaingraph.json nodes[] entry. STRICT (additionalProperties:false): every key a node uses MUST be declared here, so a typo field (e.g. gpu_fallbck) fails CI. Adding a new node field = a one-line schema update in the same PR (the §4 meta-rule applied to fields). Single-producer internal catalog — the forward-compat argument for permissive request bodies does not apply.

compute_images.description: §17/§18 — published kernel/program identities for this node. system 'sha256-source' = §17 kernel-source digest; 'risc0'/'sp1'/… = §18 zkVM ImageID/vkey.

compute_proof.description: §18 — a real, offline-produced zkVM compute-integrity receipt for this node's canonical/proven input. The worker attaches it to a live artifact only when the produced output_payload JCS-equals journal.output. Hash-excluded; never alters execution_hash or chaingraph_version.

compute_proof_ready.description: §18 tiered-rollout annotation (optional). 'deferred' = this gpu:false node has no §18 compute_proof yet and the reason is recorded in deferred_reason. Absence means no explicit annotation (a node with a compute_proof is implicitly ready). Advisory; hash-excluded.

deferred_reason.description: Why compute_proof_ready is 'deferred' (e.g. guest-capability gap or awaiting a runtime decision).

deadline.description: ISO date, or null when N/A. Catalog convention: present-as-null rather than omitted.

feeds_stub.description: Planned downstream tool_ids not yet live.

al_id.description: ApexLogics sister-suite tool id (e.g. AL-97, AL-06+16). Optional; sister-suite catalogs only.

all_mandate_types.description: All AP2 mandate types a node emits (ApexLogics multi-mandate tools).

data_vintage.description: Data vintage label, or null when N/A. Present-as-null convention.

standards_basis.description: OCG Standard §30, additive — record stays 0.8.13, no version bump — OPTIONAL self-declaration of whether this node implements a published external standard/regulation. check-clause-digest.mjs REQUIRES this field on every NEW/CHANGED node (branch-aware; pre-existing untouched nodes are reported as a gap, never retro-failed). "implements_standard" additionally requires a non-empty cited_clause_digest[]; "not_applicable" is an explicit opt-out (pure math/format-conversion nodes) and requires nothing further. "cites_informative" (added NODE-CITATION-CLASS-FIX-1, 2026-08-20): citations are retrieval provenance only; the node makes no conformance claim against the cited text; SIDEBYSIDE and PROVE gates treat it as non-standards-implementing. It additionally requires a non-empty cited_clause_digest[] (a provenance class, not an opt-out). Absence on a pre-existing node means no explicit declaration was ever made, not that the node is exempt.

cited_clause_digest.description: OCG Standard §30, additive — record stays 0.8.13, no version bump — OPTIONAL retrieval-provenance records. REQUIRED non-empty when standards_basis is "implements_standard" on a NEW/CHANGED node (check-clause-digest.mjs). Proves retrieval happened; does NOT prove the retrieved text was read correctly (§30.2) — a gate satisfied by this field alone is not a claim about interpretation accuracy.

scope_statement.description: STANDING-ORDERS #39(b)/RIDER-KERNEL, additive — record stays 0.8.13, no version bump — OPTIONAL prose statement of what a standards-implementing node does and does not compute, distinguishing it from adjacent rules and stating taxonomy honesty (class B vs class A) where applicable.

float_sensitive.description: STANDING-ORDERS #39(b)/RIDER-KERNEL, additive — record stays 0.8.13, no version bump — OPTIONAL declaration of whether the node's arithmetic is sensitive to floating-point rounding mode/precision choices, gating whether rounding_steps is expected.

rounding_steps.description: STANDING-ORDERS #39(b)/RIDER-KERNEL, additive — record stays 0.8.13, no version bump — OPTIONAL enumeration of each arithmetic rounding/precision decision the kernel makes, with its clause authority or a declared clause-silent oracle (P27/P28 anti-fabrication and step-parity properties).

cited_clause_source.description: STANDING-ORDERS #38, additive — record stays 0.8.13, no version bump — OPTIONAL flat list of publisher source URLs the node's citations were retrieved from, a display-oriented companion to the structured cited_clause_digest[] records.

clause_retrieved_date.description: STANDING-ORDERS #38, additive — record stays 0.8.13, no version bump — OPTIONAL ISO date (or semicolon-joined list) the node's cited primary text was retrieved.

clause_snapshot_location.description: STANDING-ORDERS #38, additive — record stays 0.8.13, no version bump — OPTIONAL workspace-root research/clause-snapshots/ path(s) (semicolon-joined) where the node's pinned primary-text snapshot(s) live.

cited_clause_paragraphs.description: STANDING-ORDERS #38, additive — record stays 0.8.13, no version bump — OPTIONAL human-readable list of the specific paragraph/article references the node's behaviour cites, one entry per rule or design decision.

cycle_preflight.description: GPU-CYCLE-PREFLIGHT-1, additive — record stays 0.8.13, no version bump — OPTIONAL classification of the node's measured GPU proving cost: FAST, SLOW, or PENDING when the exec-only cycle preflight harness was unreachable at authoring time.

pageless.description: OCG Standard §NODEPAGE-1, additive — record stays 0.8.13, no version bump — OPTIONAL waiver declaring that this node has NO composer page of its own; the value is the prose reason the waiver was taken. What it LICENSES: the axis-(d) node-page requirement of scripts/check-node-complete.mjs is satisfied WITHOUT a page. What it does NOT license: it is not an exemption from nav reachability for a page that DOES exist, not an exemption from the required url member, and not an exemption from the §15 catalog-parity rule that a live node's url resolves. A FALSE declaration is a HARD FAIL, machine-checked and never taken on trust: chaingraph/standard/check-pageless-consistency.mjs recomputes page existence from the filesystem and rejects any node declaring pageless while a page it owns exists (canonical chaingraph/<tool_id>.html, or its own url resolving to an .html under chaingraph/ or tools/). Absence is the default and means the node is expected to carry a page.

citedClauseDigestEntry.description: OCG Standard §30, additive — record stays 0.8.13, no version bump — one retrieval-provenance record: proof a node's behaviour was derived from a specific, retrieved primary-text clause, distinct from the §1.2 pinned-citation-to-computation binding. digest MUST be the sha256 of a CLAUSE-LEVEL snapshot excerpt, never a whole-document/whole-PDF hash (§30.1) — enforced structurally, not by convention: only a digest registered via chaingraph/standard/pin-clause-snapshot.mjs (which rejects any excerpt above its size cap) can pass check-clause-digest.mjs's registry-membership check.

digest.description: sha256 of the clause-level snapshot excerpt this node's behaviour was derived from. MUST resolve to an entry in chaingraph/standard/clause-snapshot-registry.json.

source_url.description: Publisher URL the snapshot was retrieved from.

retrieved_at.description: ISO date the snapshot was retrieved.

clause_path.description: Paragraph/section reference this node implements, e.g. "(a)(2)" or "ASU 2023-09 para 26".

scheme.description: Optional instrument scheme, reusing §1.2's open enum (cfr, eli, fasb-asu, oecd-guidance, other, ...).

chain.description: A chaingraph.json chains[] entry (live shape — the old A3 node_id/page_url schema was never adopted).

id.description: OCG §21.4 (v0.8) OPTIONAL step id (defaults to tool_id; MUST be unique within a GATED chain). Gate targets reference step ids.
